sentences.text: The present petition has been filed challenging the impugned FIR dated 15.6.2023 registered at Case Crime No. 0149 of 2023, under Sections 420, 406, 389, 506 IPC, P.S. George Town, District City Commissionarate, Prayagraj against the petitioners.

4. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the petitioner met with Imran Ahmad (respondent no.
4)/complainant through the Jeevansathi.com app for marriage.

After that, both started seeing each other, and reportedly, some financial transactions also occurred between the parties before the scheduled date of marriage; in between, the relationship got worse, and the parties landed into criminal litigation.

5. The counsel for the petitioner submits that the impugned FIR is off-suit of FIR No. 257/2023, u/s 376 I.P.C., registered at P.S. Dariyaganj Netaji Subhash Marg, New Delhi against the respondent no.
4.

The counsel further contends that the allegations of demand of three bedroom flat at Delhi by the petitioner no. 1 from the complainant and extortion of money are vague and have been levelled as a counterblast to the preceding FIR of rape registered against the complainant at Delhi.
He further contends that the petitioner bears no criminal case and is of clean antecedents.
6. Per contra, the counsel for the complainant has also entered his appearance and filed a counter affidavit in response to the allegation made in the instant petition.
The counsel submits that the petitioner is a lady of dubious character.

She and her mother uploaded false and misleading information on the Jeevansathi website by concealing the applicant's marital status to lure an innocent unmarried person for extortion of money in the guise of marriage.
The petitioner has claimed herself to be an unmarried woman.
In contrast, she married Vinod Kumar in 2015 by converting to a Hindu religion.
After the solemnization of marriage, she filed an FIR No. 237 of 2016, under Section 328/376/506 I.P.C. at P.S. Jaitpur, Delhi.
The said Vinod Kumar was sent to jail, and after that, after taking a huge amount, the matter was settled.

By adopting the same modus oprendi, the petitioner has filed similar FIR No. 257/2023, u/s 376 I.P.C., registered at P.S.
Dariyaganj Netaji Subhash Marg, New Delhi, against the complainant at New Delhi.
The counsel further contends that to some extent, the petitioner has also become successful in luring and extorting a substantial amount from him.

Lastly, he contends that the petitioner has not approached this Court with clean hands and concealed the material facts to clandestinely invite the extra ordinary jurisdiction vests with the Court under Article 226 of the Constitution.

7. Learned A.G.A. submits that on perusal of the CCTV camera footage, the presence of the petitioner, her mother and other relatives are established at the residence of the complainant, an investigation is in progress, and all evidence is being looked into to take the investigation to a logical end.

8. Be that as it may, it's not judicious for this Court to test the veracity of the allegation made in the impugned FIR, admittedly the parties are into criminal litigation, and the complainant by way of an affidavit, has also relied upon FIR No. 237 of 2016, under Section 328/376/506 I.P.C. at P.S.
Jaitpur, Delhi against Vinod Kumar whereas the petitioner has also relied upon FIR No. 257/2023,
u/s 376 I.P.C., registered at P.S. Dariyaganj Netaji Subhash Marg, New Delhi against the complainant at New Delhi.
The investigation of the impugned FIR is in progress.
